originalTitle: Dated matching and one-sided variation imply a square-root discrepancy bound
originalHypotheses: One fixed matching on all actual residual tokens, with constant endpoint ratio κ.
O(N) unmatched counts in both √N window directions.
O(n) matching crossings at every cut.
A constant upper bound on Q(q)−Q(q−1). These canonical suppliers remain open.
independence: Proof reconstructed from primary arguments and explicit definitions. Earlier source status/review assertions were not treated as proof. The author previously collected these sources; the present derivations and finite/exact-algebra checks are new independent audit work.
detailedDerivation: The degree≤2 completed graph satisfies 2Σ_inside sign=Σ_inside sign(2−degree)+Σ_boundary sign(inside endpoint). An internal opposite-sign edge cancels; each boundary edge contributes its inside sign.

Ordered-cycle crossing control gives O(N) cut counts at either end of a√N-window. UnmatchedO(N) and bounded singleton endpoints give O(N) total intrinsic defect. Therefore |Σ_window(Q+2)|≤CN in both orientations.
With Q(q)−Q(q−1)≤K, backward values obey Q(N−j)≥Q(N)−Kj; forward values obey Q(N+j)≤Q(N)+Kj. Replacing K by max(K,0) if needed preserves the premise.
Summing L=ceil√N terms in the backward and forward windows gives Q(N)≤CN/L+K(L−1)/2−2 and −Q(N)≤CN/L+K(L−1)/2+2. Hence Q=O(√N).

Edges jumping across the full window have no inside endpoint, but counting both boundary cuts only enlarges an upper bound. The initial finite exceptions are absorbed into C. Every canonical matching/endpoint/crossing/increment supplier remains a premise.
